claims.text: Nanoprecipitate coherence is the single dominant microstructural feature governing high-temperature plastic strain and toughness in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
Highly coherent nanoprecipitates facilitate dislocation transmission.
Highly coherent nanoprecipitates provide effective crack shielding.
The dislocation-transmission and crack-shielding effects of coherent nanoprecipitates enhance ductility and delay fracture under fusion-relevant thermal conditions.
The as-processed tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy contains coherent nanoprecipitates.
Targeted thermal treatments can systematically alter nanoprecipitate coherence while preserving composition and a sufficiently similar microstructure.
Temperatures of approximately 0.5–0.6 Tm, high heat flux, and reactor-representative stress states constitute relevant simulated fusion plasma-facing conditions.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces are characterized by perfect lattice matching, whereas partially or fully incoherent interfaces have reduced matching.
Low-energy coherent interfaces reduce stress concentrations and facilitate slip.
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as barriers to crack initiation.
A combination of plasticity-related and crack-shielding mechanisms can enhance ductility and toughness in a high-entropy alloy.
Samples retaining high nanoprecipitate coherence will have greater high-temperature plastic strain than the as-processed baseline.
Samples retaining high nanoprecipitate coherence will have greater toughness than the as-processed baseline.
Reducing nanoprecipitate coherence will reduce high-temperature ductility and toughness.
The hypothesized coherence-controlled behavior applies to tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys under fusion-relevant high-temperature conditions.
The hypothesis applies only when coherence is altered without major compositional or phase changes.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as already having initially coherent nanoprecipitates, yet samples that merely maintain high coherence are predicted to improve relative to that baseline. No higher coherence level or other distinguishing change is specified.
